Summary: Paul's thought command: whatever things are true, honest, just, pure, lovely, and of good report — think on these things.
Commandment: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
Application: The mind is given a menu, not a vacuum: attention is itself obedience. What is dwelt on becomes what is done, which is why the verse follows 'those things do'.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: to train attention, since thought is the seedbed of action.
